title: 用光推動的奈米機器人，把藥物送進大腦
paras: Engineers at Caltech have built tiny robots that can carry medicine into the brain. The brain is protected by the blood-brain barrier, a tight wall of cells that keeps most harmful things out. It also blocks most drugs. The new robots, called BrainBots, are about 250 nanometers wide, far smaller than a human hair.

Each robot holds a small amount of fuel behind a gate that melts when it gets warm. Near-infrared light shone through the skull opens the gate, and gas pushes the robot forward. In tests on mice with brain cancer, the robots delivered about five times more medicine and slowed tumor growth. The team says more studies are needed before trying this in people.

questions.q: Why is it hard for most drugs to reach the brain?
options: The brain is too far from the heart
The brain has no blood vessels
questions.why: 第一段：大腦有血腦屏障保護，它擋住有害物質，也擋住大部分藥物。

questions.q: What makes the gate on each robot open?
options: A magnet held near the head
questions.why: 第二段：閘門遇熱會融化，醫生用近紅外光照射穿過頭骨，閘門就打開。

questions.q: What is true about the tests so far?
options: They were done on mice, not people
They cured cancer in many patients
They showed no change in tumors
questions.why: 第二段：目前在得腦癌的老鼠身上測試，團隊說用在人身上之前還需要更多研究。
